title: Fuel and Throttle Component Locations — 3.7L Duratec
introduction:
I use this 3.7L Duratec drawing to put names to the parts handling incoming air and fuel. Follow the engine’s leader lines to the adjacent table: the throttle body is at the front of the intake, the fuel rails extend along the engine banks, and the injectors sit beneath the rails.

The throttle body contains the valve controlling how much air enters. With electronic throttle control, accelerator movement is a request to the controller rather than a cable simply pulling that valve. The rails supply fuel to the electrically controlled injectors, which meter delivery. Air and fuel meet in the engine’s work, but their controls are not interchangeable—turning up the kitchen tap does not open the window.

The separate cabin view locates the fuel pump driver module (FPDM). Use that view’s own table and its left-hand rear-seat landmark; the module’s location is distinct from the engine-mounted fuel components. The transparent views reveal relationships through surrounding parts, not the steps needed to reach them.

This is a component overview, not a fuel-pressure test or removal procedure. It supplies no seat-cushion release method or electrical test connections. If subsequent work will open the fuel system, obtain the applicable pressure-release procedure first: fuel can remain pressurized in the rail after shutdown.

edits.why: This heading keeps the engine applicability beside the view of the throttle body, injectors and rails. Component resemblance alone is not a basis for using another engine’s service instructions.
FPDM means fuel pump driver module. The cabin reference identifies its location beneath the rear seat cushion on the LH side; it does not provide the cushion-removal sequence.
